lead: Ramaphosa is sending 510 soldiers to KwaZulu-Natal after looting and violence in eThekwini, with local elections five days away; Acting Police Minister Cachalia wants KZN commissioner Mkhwanazi to head the Hawks.

items.title: Ramaphosa deploys 510 soldiers to KZN after eThekwini looting
items.summary: Speaking at the Durban Chamber of Commerce gala, the President said looting of small businesses and a killing in the Durban CBD would not be tolerated. SANDF members will back Operation Prosper in the province until the end of November.

items.title: Cachalia moves to make KZN's Mkhwanazi the new Hawks head
items.summary: The acting police minister has sent Cabinet a memorandum seeking its agreement to appoint Lt-Gen Nhlanhla Mkhwanazi, now KZN police commissioner, as national DPCI head. Lt-Gen Siphesihle Nkosi is currently acting in the post.

items.title: Durban named centre of SA's bid for the 2036 or 2040 Olympics
items.summary: Sascoc picked Durban over Johannesburg and Cape Town, with Moses Mabhida Stadium as the main venue in a likely multi-city bid. The IOC deadline to declare interest is 31 October; no cost estimate has been given yet.

items.title: Election week: matric exams pause and Sassa shifts grant dates
items.summary: NSC exams stop from 3 to 5 November around Wednesday's local elections and resume on 6 November. Sassa pays older persons' grants today, disability grants on 2 November and child grants on 3 November.

items.title: Ramaphosa brushes off polls predicting ANC slump in local elections
items.summary: Campaigning in KwaZulu-Natal, the ANC leader said the party would do well on 4 November despite forecasts of losses. eThekwini is among several metros expected to see close races, with the MK Party challenging the ANC in the province.

items.title: 2022 flood victims receive homes at Cornubia
items.summary: Houses were handed over to families displaced by the 2022 floods, and Ramaphosa said all 460 planned homes should be done by mid-2027. A second phase of 145 houses is under way.

items.title: KZN cuts projected overspending by R7.2bn
items.summary: The province's expected year-end overrun has dropped from about R9.7bn to around R2.5bn after tighter controls and a recovery plan. Finance MEC Francois Rodgers said pressure remains in health, education and public works.

items.title: Sars searches home of Tshwane finance chief
items.summary: The City of Tshwane confirmed the revenue service executed a search warrant at the home of CFO Gareth Mnisi on Thursday morning.

items.title: Spain high-speed train crash kills at least 68
items.summary: A Madrid-Seville train ran into the back of a stationary train near Urda in Toledo province on Wednesday after a signalling failure. PM Pedro Sánchez declared three days of mourning; it is Spain's second major rail disaster this year.

items.title: Israel election ends in deadlock
items.summary: Final results give Netanyahu's Likud 27 seats and Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar 21, with neither bloc reaching the 61 needed. Arab-led parties won 19 seats, and coalition talks could take weeks.

items.title: Tankers hit mines near Hormuz as oil slick reaches UAE
items.summary: Iranian officials say three tankers caught fire after striking sea mines, and a spill over 20 miles long has reached northern UAE beaches. Iran's foreign minister says he is in touch with mediators on a seven-day plan to reopen the strait.

items.title: Putin hosts African leaders at Russia-Africa summit
items.summary: Delegations from 48 African countries, 22 led by heads of state, met in Moscow. Putin said Russia would not pursue neo-colonialism and offered to widen grain and food exports to the continent.

items.title: Ethiopia takes delivery of 12 Russian Su-35 jets
items.summary: PM Abiy Ahmed said the fighters arrived a year early and that four S-400 air defence batteries will follow. Fighting continues in Tigray and Amhara.

items.title: Producer inflation jumps to 6.2% in September
items.summary: Factory-gate inflation rose from 5% in August, ahead of the roughly 5.7% economists expected. The rand eased about 0.3% to around R16.65 per dollar as gold and platinum fell after the US Fed held rates.

items.title: Big petrol hike looms for 4 November
items.summary: Mid-month Central Energy Fund data pointed to petrol rising about R1.84-R1.88 a litre and diesel about R1.25-R1.29, driven by oil near $100 a barrel. Official prices are still to be announced.

items.title: Credit and money growth slow; month-end data due today
items.summary: Private-sector credit growth eased to 6.23% in September and M3 money supply to 7.93%. Trade and budget balance figures are scheduled for release today.

items.title: Motsepe earned over R28m in final months as ARM executive chair
items.summary: African Rainbow Minerals' annual report shows his pay for the 2026 financial year before he became non-executive chair in February. ARM's headline earnings rose 19% to R3.2bn.

items.title: Proteas 40 ahead with six wickets left in Newlands Test
items.summary: After Australia made 429 for a 100-run first-innings lead, South Africa reached 140/4 at stumps on day three. Marques Ackerman scored 62 and Simon Harmer took 4/104; day four starts today.

items.title: Springboks open November tour against Italy on 7 November
items.summary: The Boks play Italy in Turin, France in Paris on 13 November and Ireland in Dublin on 21 November, before the Nations Championship finals weekend in London.

items.title: Liverpool and Man City through in Carabao Cup on penalties
items.summary: Liverpool beat Chelsea 6-5 on penalties after a 1-1 draw, and City edged Brighton in a shootout. In Serie A, Genoa beat Juventus 2-0 and Bologna won 4-2 at Milan.

items.title: Google unveils Gemini 4 Carbon for cyber-defence work
items.summary: The model targets finding and fixing software vulnerabilities and is restricted to selected security teams at first. Alphabet also reported quarterly revenue of $127.6bn, up 25%.
